paragraphs: Miller Industries, Inc., a Tennessee corporation, is The World's Largest Manufacturer of Towing and Recovery Equipment®, with executive offices in Ooltewah, Tennessee, domestic manufacturing operations in Tennessee and Pennsylvania, and foreign manufacturing operations in France, the United Kingdom and, most recently, Italy. On December 2, 2025, Miller Industries, Inc. acquired Omars – S.p.A ("Omars"), a designer and manufacturer of towing and recovery vehicles, headquartered in Cuneo, Italy.

Miller Industries was founded in 1990. Since its inception, the Company has developed innovative high-quality towing and recovery equipment worldwide. We design and manufacture bodies of car carriers and wreckers, which are installed on chassis manufactured by third parties, and sold to our customers. Our products are marketed and sold primarily through a network of distributors that serve all 50 states, Canada, Mexico, and other foreign markets, and through prime contractors to governmental entities. Further, we have substantial distribution capabilities in Europe as a result of our ownership of Jige International S.A., Boniface Engineering, Ltd, and Omars. While most of our distributor agreements do not generally contain exclusivity provisions, management believes that more than 90 percent of our independent distributors do not offer products of any other towing and recovery equipment manufacturer, which we believe is a testament of their loyalty to our brands.

In addition to selling our products, our independent distributors provide end-users with parts and service. We also utilize sales representatives to inform prospective end-users about our current product lines in an effort to drive sales to independent distributors. Management believes the strength of our distribution network and the breadth and quality of our product offerings are two key advantages over our competitors.
In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the words "Miller Industries", the "Company", "we", "our", "ours", and "us" refer to Miller Industries, Inc., and its subsidiaries.
We have acquired a number of businesses over the years that have enhanced our products portfolio.

Most recently, during fiscal 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of Omars – S.p.A, a designer and manufacturer of towing and recovery vehicles. Omars, headquartered in Cuneo, Italy, has over 45 years of experience in manufacturing light-duty, medium-duty, and heavy-duty recovery vehicles and car carriers. With a highly complementary product portfolio, management believes this acquisition will expand Miller Industries' footprint in the European market with an additional, well-recognized European brand. This acquisition will provide Miller Industries with additional capacity which the Company expects will improve its manufacturing flexibility and its ability to meet growing customer demands.

During fiscal 2023, the Company acquired substantially all of the assets and assumed certain liabilities of Southern Hydraulic Cylinder, Inc. through an acquisition subsidiary formed as a Tennessee corporation, which then changed its name to SHC, Inc. ("SHC"). SHC manufactures, sells, and services hydraulic cylinders and related components. The operations of SHC align with those of the Company, which has enhanced the stability of the Company's supply chain since the acquisition.
Our strategy has always been to enhance and diversify our product line, and we remain open to opportunities for acquisitions. We expect to continue to pursue additional acquisitions in the future.
For further information on the acquisitions, see Note 2 – "Business Combinations" to our consolidated financial statements.

Car carriers are specialized flat-bed vehicles with hydraulic tilt mechanisms that enable a towing operator to drive or winch a vehicle onto the bed for transport. Car carriers are used to transport new or disabled vehicles and other equipment, and are particularly effective for transporting vehicles or other equipment over longer distances. In addition to transporting vehicles, car carriers may also be used for other
4 | FY 2025 FORM 10-K PART I ITEM 1. BUSINESS
purposes, such as transportation of industrial equipment. Most professional towing operators have car carriers in their fleets to complement their towing capabilities.

Wreckers are generally used to recover and tow disabled vehicles and other equipment, and range in type from the conventional tow truck to large recovery vehicles with up to 100-ton lifting capacities. Wreckers are available with specialized features, including underlifts, L-arms, crossbars, and scoops, which lift disabled vehicles by the tires or front axle to minimize front-end damage to the towed vehicles. Certain heavy-duty wrecker models offer rotating booms and remote-control devices which allow heavy-duty wreckers to recover vehicles from any angle. In addition, certain light-duty wreckers are equipped with automatic wheel-lift hookup devices that allow operators to engage a disabled or unattended vehicle without leaving the cab of the wrecker.

Our wreckers range in capacity from 4 to 100 tons, and are classified as either light-duty or heavy-duty, with wreckers of 16-ton or greater capacity being classified as heavy-duty. Light-duty wreckers are used for general recovery, as well as, removing vehicles from accident scenes, and vehicles that are illegally parked, abandoned, or disabled. Heavy-duty wreckers are used in towing and recovery operations including overturned tractor trailers, buses, motor homes, and other large vehicles.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Operations

Demand from our customers and towing operators is affected by the availability of capital and access to credit, as well as rising costs of equipment ownership (including as a result of rising insurance costs).
Increases in the cost of skilled labor could adversely impact our business and profitability.
Our sales to U.S. and other governmental entities through prime contractors are subject to special risks.
Overall demand from our customers may be affected by increases in their fuel costs and changes in weather conditions.
Our competitors could impede our ability to attract or retain customers.
Our brands and reputation are dependent on the continued participation and level of service of our numerous independent distributors.
The catastrophic loss of one of our manufacturing facilities could harm our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We have made acquisitions in the past, and we remain open to opportunities to make acquisitions in the future, which could involve certain risks and uncertainties.
Risks Related to Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Matters
Environmental and health and safety liabilities and requirements could require us to incur material costs.
Failure to comply with domestic and foreign anti-corruption laws could have an adverse effect on our business.
Our future success depends upon our ability to develop or acquire proprietary products and technology and assertions against us relating to intellectual property rights could harm our business.
The effects of regulations relating to conflict minerals may adversely affect our business.
Our stock price may fluctuate greatly as a result of the general volatility of the stock market, or from our involvement with activist shareholders.
Our charter and bylaws contain anti-takeover provisions that may make it more difficult or expensive to acquire us in the future or may negatively affect our stock price.
We cannot assure you that we will continue to declare dividends on our common stock.
A disruption in, or breach in security of, information technology ("IT") systems that we use, or any violation of data protection laws, could adversely impact our business and operations.

We leverage artificial intelligence in our business, which could result in reputational harm, competitive harm, and legal liability, and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Any loss of the services of our key executives could have a material adverse impact on our operations.
paragraphs: In addition to the information discussed elsewhere in this Form 10-K, you should carefully consider the following risk factors, as well as additional factors not presently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial, which could materially affect our business, liquidity, financial condition, and/or results of operations in future periods.

Our dependence upon outside suppliers for component parts, chassis and raw materials, including aluminum, steel, and petroleum-related products, leaves us subject to changes in price and availability (including as a result of tariffs), the cadence and quantity of deliveries from our suppliers, and delays in receiving supplies of such materials, component parts or chassis.

We are dependent upon outside suppliers for our raw material needs, other purchased component parts, and chassis. Prices, availability and the timing of delivery of these raw materials, purchased component parts, and chassis are subject to substantial fluctuations that are beyond our control due to factors such as changing economic conditions, the level of tariffs that the U.S. imposes on imported steel, aluminum, and other commodities or component parts, any retaliatory actions taken by foreign governments and any resulting trade wars, inflation, governmental regulations (including CARB's Advanced Clean Trucks regulation), currency and commodity price fluctuations, resource availability, transportation costs, weather conditions or events and natural disasters, civil and political unrest and instability, acts of terrorism, war (such as the ongoing military conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine) and other factors impacting supply and demand pressures. Sporadic deliveries, significantly elevated delivery quantities, and delays in shipments of our raw materials, purchased component parts, including chassis, and government actions related to tariffs on imports and trade policies have previously adversely impacted, and have the potential to further impact our revenues, results of operations and financial condition.

As a result of our supply chain challenges in recent years, it has become more difficult to accurately forecast, purchase, warehouse, and transport - to our manufacturing facilities and to our distribution partners - purchased materials, component parts, and chassis at optimal volumes. If we are unable to accurately match the timing and quantities of component purchases, including chassis, to our actual needs or successfully manage our inventory or our workforce to adapt to the increased complexity in our supply chain, we may incur unexpected inventory buildup in our distribution channel. A mismatch in the timing and quantities of component purchases, including with respect to chassis, that results in a significant inventory buildup in our distribution channel has resulted, and could continue to result, in reduced sales, as our distribution partners work through any such inventory buildup in the field. In addition, if we experience shortages or delays in receiving raw materials, component parts, and chassis, we may also incur unexpected production disruption, as well as storage, transportation, and labor costs, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations. In addition, we may not be able to meet our customers' delivery schedules and could face the loss of orders or customers as a result of any resulting production disruptions.

Our third-party suppliers' ability to supply us with component parts and chassis is limited by their available capacity to manufacture the component parts and chassis we require, and to secure adequate freight capacity to deliver them to our facilities. Various supply chain disruptions in 2024 continued to impact our ability to obtain certain raw materials, purchased component parts and chassis from third party suppliers, resulting in substantial price increases through the third quarter of 2025. Additionally, in the fourth quarter of 2023 and during 2024, we and, in turn, our distribution partners, also experienced significantly elevated levels of chassis shipments earlier than expected that resulted in a buildup of inventory in our distribution channel during the first half of 2024. While we slowed chassis deliveries in the second half of 2024 and throughout 2025 to allow our distributor network to work through the inventory already in the distribution channel, we could continue to experience such difficulties in 2026. These supply chain difficulties have had, and are anticipated to continue to have, a material adverse impact on our profitability and results of operations.

Delays in deliveries of our finished products due to delays of purchased component parts and chassis used in our products could also adversely affect future demand for our products if our customers reduce their purchase levels with us and/or seek alternative solutions to meet their demand. If these delays, limitations on availability and price increases for raw materials, purchased component parts, and chassis continue, recur or worsen, they will continue to have a material adverse effect on production at our facilities.

PART II ITEM 7. MD&A ABOUT MILLER INDUSTRIES

Miller Industries, headquartered in Ooltewah, Tennessee, was formed in 1990 and has become The World's Largest Manufacturer of Towing and Recovery Equipment®, with domestic manufacturing operations in Tennessee and Pennsylvania, and foreign manufacturing operations in France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. Miller Industries operates as a single reportable segment and management evaluates performance on a consolidated basis. For more information, see Note 1 – "Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies".

We develop innovative high-quality towing and recovery equipment worldwide. We design and manufacture bodies of car carriers and wreckers, which are installed on chassis manufactured by third parties, and sold to our customers under our Century®, Vulcan®, Chevron™, Holmes®, Challenger®, Champion®, Jige™, Boniface™, Omars™, Titan®, and Eagle® brand names.

Our products are marketed and sold primarily through a network of distributors that serve all 50 states, Canada, Mexico, and other foreign markets, and through prime contractors to governmental entities. Further, we have substantial distribution capabilities in Europe as a result of our ownership of Jige International S.A., Boniface Engineering, Ltd, and Omars. While most of our distributor agreements do not generally contain exclusivity provisions, management believes that more than 90 percent of our independent distributors do not offer products of any other towing and recovery equipment manufacturer, which we believe is a testament of their loyalty to our brands.

In addition to selling our products, our independent distributors provide end-users with parts and service. We also utilize sales representatives to inform prospective end-users about our current product lines in an effort to drive sales to independent distributors. Management believes the strength of our distribution network and the breadth and quality of our product offerings are two key advantages over our competitors.

We focus on a variety of key indicators to monitor our overall operating and financial performance. These indicators include measurements of revenue, operating income, gross margin, net income, earnings per share, capital expenditures, and cash flow.

Our history of innovation in the towing and recovery industry has been an important factor behind our growth over the last decade, and we believe that our continued emphasis on research and development will be a key factor in our future growth. We opened a free-standing research and development facility in Chattanooga, Tennessee in 2019, where we pursue various innovations in our products and manufacturing processes, some of which are intended to enhance the safety of our employees and reduce our environmental impact. Our investments in strategic and planned projects have contributed to our increased production capacity and optimized our manufacturing processes, including investing in component re-design capabilities that allow for more flexibility in our manufacturing and sourcing. In addition, our strategic investment in Southern Hydraulic Cylinder, Inc. in May 2023, allowed us to strengthen our efforts to enhance the stability of our supply chain. Our domestic plant expansion and modernization projects have installed sophisticated robotics systems and other advanced technologies to complement our talented workforce. As we continue to focus on modernization and operational excellence, we expect to continue to invest in robotics and automated material handling equipment across all our domestic and foreign manufacturing facilities.

In March 2025, our Board of Directors authorized approximately $9.1 million (€8.0 million) for an expansion at one of our facilities in France. During the second half of 2025, work was performed to prepare the site and finalize the design. Construction for this project is expected to commence during the second quarter of 2026.

In March 2026, our Board of Directors authorized a plant expansion at our Ooltewah, TN facility, which we expect will improve our flexibility and enhance production capacity. We anticipate the cost of this project to be approximately $100.0 million and for the building project to commence in late 2026.

paragraphs: Miller Industries, Inc., 一間田納西州公司，為全球最大的拖吊與救援設備製造商®，總部設於田納西州奧爾特瓦，國內製造業務於田納西州與賓夕法尼亞州進行，國際製造業務則於法國、英國，以及最近更進軍義大利。於 2025 年 12 月 2 日，Miller Industries, Inc. 收購 Omars – S.p.A ("Omars")，一家拖吊與救援車輛的設計與製造商，總部設於義大利庫內奧。

Miller Industries 於 1990 年成立。自成立以來，本公司已在全球開發創新且高品質的拖吊與救援設備。我們設計與製造車載拖吊與救援車的車身，這些車身安裝於第三方製造的車架上，並銷售給客戶。我們的產品主要透過遍佈美國 50 州、加拿大、墨西哥及其他國際市場的經銷商網路進行行銷與銷售，並透過主要承包商銷售給政府機構。此外，我們因擁有 Jige International S.A.、Boniface Engineering, Ltd 及 Omars 而在歐洲擁有廣泛的經銷能力。雖然大多數經銷商契約通常不包含獨佔條款，但管理層認為超過 90% 的獨立經銷商並未銷售任何其他拖吊與救援設備製造商的產品，我們認為這顯示他們對我們品牌的忠誠度。
除了銷售我們的產品，我們的獨立經銷商也為最終用戶提供零件與服務。我們也使用銷售代表向潛在最終用戶介紹我們的現有產品線，以促進銷售至獨立經銷商。管理層認為我們的經銷網路強度與產品線的廣度與品質是我們對抗競爭對手的兩大優勢。
在本年度報告表 10-K 中，"Miller Industries"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們的"、"我們的"及"我們"均指 Miller Industries, Inc. 及其子公司。
我們已多年來收購多家公司，這些收購已增強我們的產品組合。

最近，於財務年度 2025，本公司完成收購 Omars – S.p.A，一家拖吊與救援車輛的設計與製造商。Omars 總部設於義大利庫內奧，擁有超過 45 年的輕型、中型及重型救援車與車載拖吊製造經驗。由於其高度補充性的產品組合，管理層認為此收購將擴大 Miller Industries 在歐洲市場的足跡，並增加一個備受認可的歐洲品牌。此收購將為 Miller Industries 提供額外的生產能力，本公司預期此將提高其生產靈活性與滿足日益增長的客戶需求的能力。
於財務年度 2023，本公司收購 Southern Hydraulic Cylinder, Inc. 的 substantially all 資產，並承擔部分負債，透過一間成立為田納西州公司的收購子公司進行，該子公司隨後更名為 SHC, Inc. ("SHC")。SHC 製造、銷售與維修液壓缸與相關零組件。SHC 的業務與本公司業務相符，自收購以來已增強本公司供應鏈的穩定性。
我們的策略始終是增強與多元化我們的產品線，我們仍對收購機會持開放態度。我們預期將持續尋求未來的更多收購機會。
有關取得之進一步資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表之附註 2 – "企業合併"。
車載運工具為專門設計的平板車輛，具備液壓傾斜機制，使拖車操作員能駕駛或使用拖車將車輛載上車廂進行運輸。車載運工具用於運輸新車或故障車輛及其他設備，尤其適合長距離運輸車輛或其他設備。除了運輸車輛外，車載運工具也可用於其他用途，例如工業設備的運輸。大多數專業拖車操作員在其車隊中皆擁有車載運工具，以補強其拖車能力。

拖車通常用來回收及拖運故障車輛及其他設備，其類型從傳統拖車到具備最高 100 噸起重能力的大型回收車輛不等。拖車可配備專門功能，包括底吊架、L 型臂、橫桿及挖掘器，這些裝置可透過車輪或前軸吊起故障車輛，以減少被拖車輛的前端損壞。某些重型拖車模型提供旋轉起重臂及遙控裝置，使重型拖車能從任何角度回收車輛。此外，某些輕型拖車則配備自動輪轄連接裝置，使操作員能在不離開拖車駕駛室的情況下連接故障或未經授權的車輛。
我們的拖車起重能力從 4 噸至 100 噸不等，並分為輕型及重型兩種，起重能力達 16 噸或以上的拖車被歸類為重型。輕型拖車用於一般回收作業，以及從事故現場、違規停放、遺棄或故障車輛中移除車輛。重型拖車用於拖車及回收作業，包括翻覆的卡車拖車、巴士、旅居車及其他大型車輛。

paragraphs: 本報告中所使用的 "Miller Industries"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們的"、"我們的"、"我們" 及其他相似代詞，均指 Miller Industries, Inc. 及其合併子公司，除非文意另有要求。我們的會計年度於 12 月 31 日結束。提及財務年度 2025、2024 及 2023，均指於 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的財務年度，除非另有說明。除另有說明外，本報告中資訊均為 2025 年 12 月 31 日之資料。為便於及時報導，合併財務報表包含某些子公司帳戶，其會計年度結算日與 12 月 31 日相差 31 天（或更短）。

本 Form 10-K 中的 MD&A 一般討論財務年度 2025 及財務年度 2024 的項目，以及財務年度 2025 與財務年度 2024 的年對年比較。財務年度 2024 的項目及未包含於本 Form 10-K 中的財務年度 2024 與財務年度 2023 年對年比較討論，可於我們 2024 年財務年度結束於 12 月 31 日的年度報告 Form 10-K 中的 Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations 部分找到（稱為 "2024 Form 10-K"）。

本報告（包括引用資料）包含展望性陳述，涉及預期、前景、估計及其他事項，這些事項依賴未來事件或發展。許多展望性陳述出現在 MD&A 及風險因素中，但本報告中也有其他展望性陳述，可能以 "may"、"will"、"should"、"could"、"continue"、"future"、"potential"、"believe"、"project"、"plan"、"intend"、"seek"、"estimate"、"predict"、"expect"、"anticipate" 及其變體及相似表達方式識別，並包含反映未來結果或指引的陳述、展望陳述及費用提列。這些事項受風險與不確定性影響，可能導致實際結果與預期、預測或暗示的結果有重大差異。這些風險與不確定性中最重要的部分，於本報告的 "風險因素" 部分有說明。本報告中的展望性陳述僅於本報告日期為準。除非法律有明確要求，否則我們不承諾更新或修正任何展望性陳述。

我們的年度報告 Form 10-K、季報 Form 10-Q、現況報告 Form 8-K 及其修正案，均可於我們的網站（www.millerind.com）上免費取得，於 "投資人 — 檔案 — 年度報告" 項目下，我們在電子提交至美國證券交易委員會（SEC）或提供給 SEC 後，盡速提供。美國證券交易委員會（SEC）也維護一個網站（www.sec.gov），您可在該網站上搜尋年度、季度及現況報告、代理書及資訊說明書，以及其他有關我們與其他上市公司的資訊。
第二部分 第七項 MD&A 關於 Miller Industries
Miller Industries 設立於田納西州奧爾特韋哈，成立於 1990 年，已成為全球最大的拖車與救援設備製造商®，擁有美國田納西州與賓夕法尼亞州的國內製造業務，以及法國、義大利與英國的海外製造業務。Miller Industries 作為單一應報告分部運作，管理階層以合併基礎評估表現。如需更多資訊，請參閱附註 1 — "組織與重要會計政策摘要"。
我們在全球開發創新且高品質的拖車與救援設備。我們設計與製造車載拖車與救援設備的車身，這些車身安裝於第三方製造的車架上，並以我們的 Century®、Vulcan®、Chevron™、Holmes®、Challenger®、Champion®、Jige™、Boniface™、Omars™、Titan® 及 Eagle® 品牌名稱銷售給客戶。

我們的產品主要透過一個覆蓋美國 50 州、加拿大、墨西哥及其他外國市場的經銷商網路進行行銷與銷售，並透過主要承包商銷售給政府機構。此外，我們因擁有 Jige International S.A.、Boniface Engineering, Ltd 及 Omars 而在歐洲擁有強大的經銷能力。雖然大多數我們的經銷商契約通常不包含獨佔條款，管理階層認為超過 90% 的我們獨立經銷商並未銷售任何其他拖車與救援設備製造商的產品，我們認為這顯示他們對我們品牌的忠誠度。
除銷售我們的產品外，我們的獨立經銷商會向終端用戶提供零組件與服務。我們也利用銷售代表向潛在終端用戶介紹我們目前的產品線，以促進銷售至獨立經銷商。管理階層認為，我們的經銷網路強度與產品種類與品質的廣度，是我們對競爭對手的兩大優勢。
我們關注多種關鍵指標以監測我們整體營運與財務表現。這些指標包括營業收入、營運收入、毛利率、淨收入、每股盈餘、資本支出與現金流量的衡量。

我們在拖吊與救援產業的創新歷史，是我們過去十年成長的重要因素，我們認為我們持續強調研究與開發將是未來成長的關鍵因素。我們於2019年在田納西州查塔努加開設了一座獨立的研究與開發設施，我們在該設施中追求各種產品與製造流程的創新，其中一些創新旨在提升我們員工的安全性並減少對環境的影響。我們在戰略與計畫專案上的投資，已提高我們的生產能力並優化製造流程，包括投資於零組件重新設計能力，使我們的製造與採購更具靈活性。此外，我們於2023年5月對Southern Hydraulic Cylinder, Inc.進行戰略投資，使我們能強化對供應鏈穩定性的努力。我們的國內工廠擴張與現代化專案已安裝先進的機械手臂系統及其他先進科技，以補強我們的優秀人才團隊。隨著我們持續著重現代化與營運卓越，我們預期會持續投資於機械手臂與自動化物料處理設備，應用於所有國內與海外製造工廠。
2025 年 3 月，本公司董事會核准約 9.1 百萬美元（€8.0 百萬）用於法國一處設施的擴建計畫。2025 年第二季期間，進行了現場準備及設計最終確定的工作。此計畫的建設預計於 2026 年第二季開始進行。
2026年3月，我們的董事會批准了位於Ooltewah, TN工廠的擴廠計畫，我們預期此計畫將提高我們的靈活性並提升生產能力。我們預期此專案的成本約為100.0 百萬美元，並預計於2026年底開始興建。
趨勢與其他影響我們業務的因素

headings: 營運相關風險
客戶及拖車運營商的訂單需求受資金可得性及信貸取得能力影響，同時也受設備擁有成本（包括因保險成本上升所致）的影響。
技能勞工成本的增加可能對本公司業務及獲利能力產生負面影響。
本公司透過主要承包商向美國及其他政府機構銷售產品，可能面臨特殊風險。
客戶總體需求可能因燃料成本上升及天氣條件變化而受到影響。
競爭對手可能阻礙本公司吸引或留住客戶的能力。
本公司品牌及聲譽依賴眾多獨立經銷商持續參與及服務水準。
本公司製造廠房發生大規模損失可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成傷害。
本公司過去曾進行過收購，並持續對未來可能的收購機會保持開放態度，此過程可能伴隨某些風險與不確定性。
與法律、法規及合規事項相關的風險
環境及健康與安全責任與要求，可能導致本公司需承擔重大成本。
未能遵守國內外反貪污法規，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司未來的成功取決於本公司開發或取得專有產品與技術的能力，而與本公司相關的智慧財產權爭議，可能對本公司業務造成損害。
與衝突礦物相關法規的影響，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司股票價格可能因股票市場整體波動，或因本公司與活躍股東的關係而大幅波動。
本公司章程及章程規則包含反併購條款，可能使未來收購本公司變得更加困難或成本更高，或可能對本公司股票價格產生負面影響。
本公司無法保證將持續於普通股上宣告紅利。
若本公司所使用的資訊科技（"IT"）系統發生中斷，或資料安全遭入侵，或違反資料保護法規，將可能對本公司業務及營運造成不利影響。
本公司於業務中運用人工智慧，可能導致聲譽損害、競爭力受損及法律責任，並對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
若喪失本公司關鍵高階主管之服務，可能對本公司營運造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 除本表單 10-K 其他處所討論之資訊外，您應謹慎考慮下列風險因素，以及目前尚未為我們所知或目前認為不重要之其他因素，這些因素可能對我們未來期間之業務、流動性、財務狀況及/或營運結果產生重大影響。
我們對外部供應商提供零組件、機殼及原材料（包括鋁、鋼及石油相關產品）之依賴，使我們面臨價格與可得性之變動（包括因關稅所致），以及供應商交付頻率與數量，以及接收這些材料、零組件或機殼之延遲。

我們依賴外部供應商來滿足我們之原材料需求、其他購入零組件及機殼。這些原材料、購入零組件及機殼之價格、可得性及交付時間，因諸如總體經濟條件變動、美國對進口鋼鐵、鋁及其它商品或零組件所施加關稅之程度、外國政府所採取之報復性行動及由此產生之貿易戰、通貨膨脹、政府規範（包括 CARB 的先進清潔貨車規範）、貨幣與商品價格波動、資源可得性、運輸成本、天氣條件或事件及自然災害、民事與政治動盪、恐怖行動、戰爭（如中東及烏克蘭持續的軍事衝突）等因素，而超出我們之控制範圍。偶發性交付、顯著提高之交付數量，以及我們原材料、購入零組件（包括機殼）及政府針對進口關稅與貿易政策之行動所導致之延遲，已先前對我們之營收、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響，且有潛在可能進一步影響我們之營收、營運結果及財務狀況。

由於我們近年來在供應鏈方面所面臨的挑戰，使我們更難以準確預測、採購、倉儲及運輸至我們之製造廠與分銷夥伴之購入材料、零組件及機殼至最佳數量。若我們無法準確匹配零組件（包括機殼）之採購時間與數量至我們實際需求，或成功管理我們之存貨或人力以適應我們供應鏈中增加的複雜性，我們可能在分銷渠道產生意外的存貨積壓。零組件（包括機殼）採購時間與數量之不匹配，導致我們分銷渠道產生顯著存貨積壓，已導致，且可能繼續導致銷售減少，因我們之分銷夥伴正在場域內處理任何此類存貨積壓。此外，若我們遭遇原材料、零組件及機殼之短缺或延遲，我們也可能面臨意外的生產中斷，以及儲存、運輸及勞動成本，這可能會對我們之財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。此外，我們可能無法符合客戶之交貨排程，並可能因任何由此產生之生產中斷而失去訂單或客戶。

我們第三方供應商供應我們零組件及機殼之能力，受限於其製造我們所需零組件及機殼之可用容量，以及取得足夠運輸容量將其運送到我們設施之能力。2024 年各種供應鏈中斷持續影響我們從第三方供應商取得特定原材料、購入零組件及機殼之能力，導致 2025 年第三季前出現顯著價格上漲。此外，在 2023 年第四季及 2024 年期間，我們及我們的分銷夥伴也經歷了比預期更早的機殼運輸數量顯著增加，導致 2024 年上半年我們分銷渠道出現存貨積壓。雖然我們在 2024 年下半年及 2025 年期間減緩機殼運輸，以讓分銷網路處理分銷渠道已有的存貨，我們仍可能在 2026 年繼續面臨此類困難。這些供應鏈困難已對我們之獲利能力及營運結果產生重大不利影響，並預期持續對我們之獲利能力及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
我們成品交付延遲，因購入零組件及機殼之延遲，也可能因客戶減少與我們之採購量及/或尋求替代方案以滿足其需求，而對我們未來產品之需求產生不利影響。若這些延遲、供應限制及原材料、購入零組件及機殼之價格上漲持續、重複或惡化，將持續對我們製造廠之生產產生重大不利影響。
